transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
If you were flying Delta Sunday, there's a good chance you were delayed.
The airline reported problems with an automated system
used to calculate weight and balance of its planes.
NPR's Andrea Shue reports 1,300 Delta flights faced delays.
For a good part of the day, Delta Airlines said it used manual workarounds
to safely get flights off the ground.
By mid-afternoon, the automation was once again working.
The airline says its re-booking passengers
and providing meals and hotel rooms were necessary.
The problems come just over a week after the Federal Aviation Administration
called a nationwide ground stop that halted takeoffs for more than four hours.
Officials said some maintenance work on an aging system was to blame.
With Thanksgiving approaching, AAA projects some 6 million people
will be flying this week.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
The annual UN Climate Talks conference in Turkey
ended in dramatic fashion without an agreement.
NPR's Julia Simon reports some are saying it was the worst conference ever.
It's the longest climate conference in history,
yet the conference ended without a deal.
The conference works by consensus, and countries disagreed
whether or not the text should mention transitioning away from fossil fuels.
Burning fossil fuels drives about 73% of planet heating emissions,
yet some countries like Saudi Arabia opposed fossil fuel language.
Frustrated with the United Nations conference,
more than 50 countries have started their own conference.
It's focused on transitioning away from oil, gas, and coal,
and will have its second convening in July.
Meanwhile, countries are already moving away from oil and gas
to solar and electric vehicles.
Not always for climate reasons, but economic ones.
Julia Simon, NPR News.
Starting January, the first work requirements are being added to Medicaid,
the public health insurance program for low-income people.
NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffins report...
Right now, Medicaid covers about 70 million low-income Americans.
About 5 million of them are projected to become uninsured
because of the new work requirements.
Adriana McIntyre is a health policy professor at Harvard.
She points out enrollment has to shrink
in order to achieve savings in the Republican budget law.
You only save money in Medicaid if you're covering fewer people.
And if you're only covering fewer healthy people,
you're not saving that much money.
It's covering fewer people who need health care.
That's where you get "savings" out of work requirements.
Democrats say reversing this policy is a top priority
when they take over the majority in Congress.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
House Democrats will have at least 258 seats in the new Congress Sunday.
A race in North Carolina was called for the Democrats.
It's NPR.
Grand Theft Auto VI bought in nearly $3.8 billion worldwide on its first day.
It's the first new game in this series in 13 years.
Players can steal cars and pull off heists in the game.
And as Vicki Barker reports from London,
the release gave police an unexpected break in a real-life criminal case.
A police force in rural Bedfordshire was one of several around the world
to ride on the promotional coattails of Grand Theft Auto VI.
Us cops, we got to protect each other.
The force shared a series of wanted posters on Facebook
using GTA-adjacent graphics featuring mugshots of six people under the heading
"Bedfordshire's Most Wanted, Level 1-6."
The post generated thousands of likes
and resulted in a tip-off that has now led to the arrest of one of the suspects
wanted in connection with multiple burglaries and thefts.
One Facebook user commented,
"Whoever's in charge of social media for Bedfordshire Police needs a raise.
This is legendary."
For NPR News, I'm Vicki Barker in London.
Tom Jackson considered one of the NFL's Denver Broncos standout players
and who later had a 29-year-long career at ESPN.
Alongside Chris Berman died Friday.
His death was announced Sunday.
Jackson was 75.
He played linebacker for 14 years in the NFL, all with Denver,
and he's in the team's Ring of Honor.
In 1986, after retiring, he joined ESPN,
and his work was recognized by the network and the NFL.
From Washington, I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News.

topics.text: Delta Airlines faces about 1,300 flight delays after automated weight and balance system failure
UN climate talks in Turkey end without agreement over fossil fuel language
Medicaid work requirements take effect in January, projected to uninsure about 5 million people
House Democrats secure at least 258 seats in the new Congress after North Carolina race call
Grand Theft Auto VI earns nearly $3.8 billion worldwide on first day of release
Bedfordshire Police use GTA-style wanted posters on Facebook, leading to a suspect's arrest
Denver Broncos linebacker Tom Jackson, later an ESPN analyst, dies at age 75
